$doc: Vyomi capability registry — Azure Monitor. One entry per console section that makes a backend claim (proven by tests/conformance/test_capabilities.py). Pure navigation/reference sections (Overview, Insights Hub) carry no backend claim and are intentionally not listed here. level.nano = core/azure_monitor_core.py + core/azure_operationalinsights_core.py in-process (Nano / dev_server, checked by this test without CAP_BASE). level.offline = the full appliance (providers/azure_services.py), which wires the SAME core modules over its own ARM resource store.

azure.monitor.alert_rules.title: Alert rules (metric + activity log alert rules: create, list, delete)

azure.monitor.action_groups.title: Action groups (create, list, delete, test notification, enable receiver)

azure.monitor.autoscale.title: Autoscale settings (create, list, delete)
limitations: Scaling never actually runs (there is no live metric stream to evaluate rules against); the setting is stored and returned exactly as configured.

azure.monitor.activity_log.title: Activity log (subscription-wide feed of real ARM writes)
limitations: Only control-plane writes Vyomi itself performs are recorded; there is no data-plane or sign-in activity.

azure.monitor.log_analytics_workspaces.title: Log Analytics workspaces (create, list, delete, keys, usage, tables)

azure.monitor.resource_insights.title: Per-resource-type Insights dashboards (Applications, Virtual Machines, Storage accounts, Networks, Azure Cosmos DB, Key Vaults, Service Bus)
limitations: Shows Vyomi's real resource inventory for the type; there is no request/exception/dependency telemetry, VM guest metrics, or health rollup — those need an agent-based collection pipeline Vyomi does not run.

azure.monitor.metrics_scope.title: Metrics — scope picker (resource types, locations)
limitations: Scope, resource-type and location pickers are real (drawn from your inventory); the chart itself is not — metric definitions/values are not modelled.

azure.monitor.monitoring_coverage.title: Monitoring Coverage (resources with vs. without an alert rule)
limitations: Coverage is approximated as "referenced by at least one alert rule's scopes"; Azure's own per-signal telemetry coverage model is not reproduced.

azure.monitor.advisor_recommendations.title: Advisor recommendations (resources with no alert rule, derived from real inventory)
limitations: Recommendations are "this resource has no alert rule", not Azure Advisor's own usage-pattern heuristics.

azure.monitor.metrics_charts.title: Metrics charts (metric definitions and time-series values)
limitations: Exactly one real metric exists per resource — "Activity operations", a genuine count of that resource's own Activity log rows (never synthetic/random data), bucketed over the requested interval.

Average/Minimum/Maximum report the same per-bucket count as Total/Count (there is only one real sample per bucket) — Azure's richer resource-specific metric catalogs (CPU, requests, throughput, …) are not reproduced.
Not simulated: Add filter, Apply splitting, Save to dashboard — Vyomi has no metric dimensions and no custom-dashboard resource to save a chart into.

azure.monitor.log_query.title: Log Analytics query (KQL)
limitations: Only a small KQL subset is understood: a table name, then any of where (==/!=/contains/startswith), project, sort by/order by, take/limit and count — unsupported syntax returns a real error instead of succeeding silently.

Only the built-in AzureActivity table has rows, and they are the subscription's real Activity log (the same Microsoft.Insights/eventtypes feed the Activity log page reads) — every other table (Heartbeat, Perf, Syslog, Event, Usage, AzureDiagnostics, any custom _CL/_RST table) is always empty: there is no agent/telemetry ingestion pipeline.

AzureActivity is not gated by a per-workspace Activity Log export / diagnostic setting (Vyomi does not model one at subscription scope) — every workspace's AzureActivity table sees the whole subscription feed.

The api.loganalytics.io data-plane host itself (azure-monitor-query / LogsQueryClient) is not modelled; the query runs over the same ARM pass-through path (.../workspaces/{ws}/api/query) the Azure Portal's Logs blade uses.

azure.monitor.observability_agents.title: Observability agents (preview)
limitations: Modelled as the real mechanic behind it — a Microsoft.Insights/dataCollectionRuleAssociations extension resource linking a VM to an existing Data Collection Rule, validated against the shared ARM store — rather than a cosmetic "agent installed" flag.
No agent process actually runs on the VM and no telemetry is ever collected or shipped; only Virtual Machines are offered (Arc-connected servers are not modelled).

azure.monitor.issues.title: Issues
limitations: Vyomi has no cross-signal (metrics + logs + availability) ML correlation engine; this groups the one real failure signal the backend produces — Activity log rows whose status isn't Succeeded — by resource.

Today the only path that ever logs a non-Succeeded row is a real ARM template deployment whose template evaluation fails (core/azure_arm_core.py); most other operations fail before being accepted and so never appear here, matching real Azure deployment semantics but not its broader anomaly detection.

azure.monitor.health_models.title: Health models
limitations: A health model is real CRUD (Microsoft.Insights/healthModels: a named collection of member resource ids); the rollup health per member is computed from the same real Activity-log failure signal Issues uses, not authored dependency/signal graphs with weighted health criteria the real feature supports.

azure.monitor.change_analysis.title: Change Analysis (derived from the real Activity log)
limitations: Change type/Name/Resource type are derived from the Activity log feed (real ARM writes), not from Azure Resource Graph's property-level snapshots — there is no before/after diff of individual properties.
Toolbar actions not simulated: Open query, Group by none.

azure.monitor.service_health.title: Service health
limitations: There is no real Azure platform behind Vyomi to go down, so a fabricated incident feed would be dishonest. Instead this lists the REAL resource provider namespaces this subscription has registered (GET /subscriptions/{sub}/providers) — every one Available, which is a true statement about this environment (no fault injection), not a canned incident list.

azure.monitor.workbooks.title: Workbooks (Gallery): create, list, delete
limitations: A workbook is stored as a name/category/serializedData document, the same shape the real resource has; there is no visual report editor to author the serializedData JSON.
Toolbar actions not simulated: New (visual editor), Feedback, Help, Community Git repo, Browse across galleries, Recycle Bin.

azure.monitor.grafana_dashboards.title: Dashboards with Grafana
limitations: Azure Managed Grafana is a separate managed service Vyomi does not run.
Toolbar actions would be New, Explore, Browse Grafana dashboards Gallery, Browse Saved dashboards, Help, Feedback, Group by.

azure.monitor.containers_insights.title: Container insights
limitations: Shows Vyomi's real AKS cluster inventory (Microsoft.ContainerService/managedClusters, the same core/azure_arm_core.py store the AKS console reads); there is no container/pod-level telemetry or log collection — that needs an agent-based collection pipeline Vyomi does not run.

azure.monitor.redis_insights.title: Azure Cache for Redis insights
limitations: Microsoft.Cache/redis is a real, generic-catalog ARM resource (control plane only — the cache instance, SKU and access keys behave like Azure); this page shows that real inventory, not a telemetry rollup (there is no Redis data-plane protocol server behind it).

azure.monitor.data_explorer_insights.title: Azure Data Explorer Clusters insights
limitations: Microsoft.Kusto/clusters is a real, generic-catalog ARM resource (control plane only — the cluster resource, SKU and state behave like Azure); this page shows that real inventory, not a telemetry rollup (there is no Kusto query engine behind it).

azure.monitor.azure_local_insights.title: Azure Local insights
limitations: Azure Local (hybrid hardware) is out of scope for a cloud simulator.

azure.monitor.managed_prometheus.title: Managed Prometheus
limitations: Azure Kubernetes Service and the managed Prometheus add-on are not modelled.
Grid columns would be Name, Resource group, Metrics collection; toolbar actions would be View manual setup, Feedback.

azure.monitor.managed_grafana.title: Azure Managed Grafana
limitations: Azure Managed Grafana is a separate managed service Vyomi does not run.

azure.monitor.scom_managed_instance.title: Azure Monitor SCOM managed instance
limitations: SCOM managed instance is out of scope for a simulator.

azure.monitor.diagnostic_settings.title: Diagnostic settings (per-resource logs/metrics routing: resource picker + create/list/delete)
limitations: Logs/metrics are never actually delivered to the configured destination (workspace, storage account or event hub) — there is no agent/telemetry pipeline, so the setting is stored and validated exactly as the real resource requires but nothing flows.

Vyomi has no catalog of a resource type's real log/metric category names (GET .../diagnosticSettingsCategories is not modelled) — the create form offers the 'allLogs' category group and 'AllMetrics' rather than a resource-specific category picker.

azure.monitor.data_collection_rules.title: Data Collection Rules (create, list, delete)
limitations: A rule's data flows and destinations are stored and validated exactly as the real resource requires; data is never actually collected or routed (there is no agent fleet to configure).
Toolbar actions not simulated: Feedback, Use preview. Summary counts not simulated: Resources collecting, Not collecting.

azure.monitor.data_collection_endpoints.title: Data Collection Endpoints (create, list, delete)
limitations: The logs/metrics/configuration ingestion endpoint URLs are generated and stable across updates, the same shape the real resource returns; nothing is ever sent to them (no agent fleet).

azure.monitor.pipelines.title: Azure Monitor pipelines (create, list, delete)
limitations: A pipeline group's platform and collector endpoints are stored and validated exactly as the real resource requires (Microsoft.Insights/pipelineGroups); no on-premises OpenTelemetry collector fleet actually runs, so nothing is ever collected or forwarded — the same "config real, data flow not" shape as Data Collection Endpoints.

azure.monitor.private_link_scopes.title: Azure Monitor Private Link Scopes (create, list, delete, access mode settings, Azure Monitor Resources)
limitations: The scope resource, its query/ingestion access-mode settings and its scoped resources (the "Azure Monitor Resources" tab — linking a Log Analytics workspace into the scope) are real and validated against the shared inventory; private endpoint connections are not modelled — Vyomi has no private networking stack.

azure.monitor.new_support_request.title: New support request (file a Microsoft support ticket)
limitations: Vyomi does not file real Microsoft support tickets.
